## Preliminary & unvetted analysis
Exploratory analysis. The comparison between datasets is observational: designs with and without
non-vanilla trials differ in lab, stimuli, age range and procedure.
:::





::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
i_am("notebooks/01-design.qmd")

RELEASE <- "2026.1"
CACHE <- here("cache", "01_peekbank_meta.rds")
ELIFE <- here("cache", "peekbank-development")
```
:::





## Inputs

Two inputs:

1. The trial-level analysis file from Frank et al. (2025), `cached_intermediates/1_d_trial.Rds`
   in [peekbank/peekbank-development](https://github.com/peekbank/peekbank-development). It holds
   **only vanilla trials** (familiar word, plain carrier phrase), English, age ≤ 60 months,
   monolingual datasets, after the paper's item and data-quality filters. We use it unchanged.
2. Peekbank's metadata tables for the same release, which list **every** trial each child saw,
   including the non-vanilla ones that the paper dropped.





::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
if (!dir.exists(ELIFE)) {
  system2("git", c("clone", "--depth", "1",
                   "https://github.com/peekbank/peekbank-development", ELIFE))
}

if (!file.exists(CACHE)) {
  library(peekbankr)
  pb <- peekbank(RELEASE)
  meta <- list(datasets = pb$datasets, administrations = pb$administrations,
               trials = pb$trials, trial_types = pb$trial_types, stimuli = pb$stimuli)
  # trials has no administration_id; the link is only in the timepoint tables
  admin_trials <- pb$db$aoi_timepoints |> distinct(administration_id, trial_id) |> collect()
  saveRDS(c(meta, list(admin_trials = admin_trials, release = RELEASE)), CACHE)
}
m <- readRDS(CACHE)
stopifnot(m$release == RELEASE)

d_trial <- readRDS(file.path(ELIFE, "cached_intermediates", "1_d_trial.Rds")) |> ungroup()
d_sub <- readRDS(file.path(ELIFE, "cached_intermediates", "1_d_sub.Rds")) |> ungroup()
```
:::





The paper's file has 58099 vanilla trials from 4124
sessions in 26 datasets.

## Every trial in each session





::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
all_trials <- m$admin_trials |>
  left_join(m$trials |> select(trial_id, trial_order, trial_type_id), by = "trial_id") |>
  left_join(m$trial_types |> select(trial_type_id, dataset_name, condition, vanilla_trial),
            by = "trial_type_id") |>
  filter(dataset_name %in% unique(d_trial$dataset_name))

session_design <- all_trials |>
  group_by(dataset_name, administration_id) |>
  summarise(n_trials_session = n(),
            n_nonvanilla_session = sum(!vanilla_trial),
            prop_nonvanilla_session = mean(!vanilla_trial),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(session_design = if_else(n_nonvanilla_session == 0, "vanilla only", "mixed")) |>
  group_by(dataset_name) |>
  mutate(dataset_design = if_else(all(n_nonvanilla_session == 0), "vanilla only", "mixed")) |>
  ungroup() |>
  left_join(read_csv(here("metadata", "nonvanilla_types.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
              select(-notes), by = "dataset_name") |>
  mutate(nonvanilla_type = if_else(session_design == "vanilla only", "none (vanilla only)",
                                   nonvanilla_type))
stopifnot(!any(is.na(session_design$nonvanilla_type)))
```
:::





Two versions of the split:

* **Dataset design**: does the dataset contain any non-vanilla trials at all?
* **Session design**: did *this child's session* contain any non-vanilla trials? This is the
  more precise coding. Four longitudinal Fernald/Marchman datasets ran vanilla-only sessions at the
  youngest ages and added other trial types later, so the two codings differ for them.

"Vanilla" follows Peekbank's `vanilla_trial` flag. It is a liberal flag: several "vanilla only"
datasets have manipulations that Peekbank still counts as vanilla (semantically related
distractors, typical vs atypical exemplars, coarticulation cues, gender-consistent speakers).
None of those involves an odd-sounding label, a novel word, or a label with no matching referent.





::: {#tbl-datasets .cell tbl-cap='Design of each dataset in the Frank et al. (2025) analysis file. Sessions and ages are for sessions that contribute vanilla trials to the analysis.'}

```{.r .cell-code}
dataset_table <- d_trial |>
  distinct(dataset_name, administration_id, age) |>
  left_join(session_design, by = c("dataset_name", "administration_id")) |>
  group_by(dataset_name, dataset_design) |>
  summarise(sessions = n(),
            `sessions vanilla only` = sum(session_design == "vanilla only"),
            `sessions mixed` = sum(session_design == "mixed"),
            `mean age (mo)` = round(mean(age), 1),
            `% non-vanilla in mixed sessions` =
              round(100 * mean(prop_nonvanilla_session[session_design == "mixed"])),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(read_csv(here("metadata", "nonvanilla_types.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE),
            by = "dataset_name") |>
  arrange(dataset_design, dataset_name)
knitr::kable(dataset_table)
```

## Position of each vanilla trial among non-vanilla trials

For the within-session analysis (@sec-within) we count, for each vanilla trial, how many
non-vanilla trials came before it in the same session, and whether the trial just before it was
non-vanilla. Trials that were never imported into Peekbank cannot be counted, so these are lower
bounds.





::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
position <- all_trials |>
  arrange(administration_id, trial_order) |>
  group_by(administration_id) |>
  mutate(n_prev = row_number() - 1,
         n_prev_nonvanilla = cumsum(!vanilla_trial) - !vanilla_trial,
         prev_nonvanilla = lag(!vanilla_trial),
         prev_condition = lag(condition)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(administration_id, trial_id, condition, n_prev, n_prev_nonvanilla, prev_nonvanilla)

trials_out <- d_trial |>
  select(dataset_name, subject_id, administration_id, trial_id, trial_order, age,
         target_label, distractor_label, short_window_accuracy, long_window_accuracy,
         rt, log_rt) |>
  left_join(session_design, by = c("dataset_name", "administration_id")) |>
  left_join(position, by = c("administration_id", "trial_id"))
stopifnot(nrow(trials_out) == nrow(d_trial), !any(is.na(trials_out$session_design)))

write_csv(trials_out, here("data", "derived", "vanilla_trials_design.csv"), na = "")
write_csv(session_design, here("data", "derived", "session_design.csv"), na = "")
```
:::





Written to `data/derived/`: `vanilla_trials_design.csv` (58099 vanilla trials with
design codes) and `session_design.csv` (one row per session).
